b2-17-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What They Say in Rome
b2-17-01.scenario: In the palace, Nero tells Seneca what he has heard about his poems in the city.
b2-17-01.prompt: As Nero, tell Seneca what you have heard, without saying that you are sure.
cues: Say that it is only a rumor
Say what people do in the city
b2-17-01.target: Úgy hírlik, hogy a városban nevetnek rajtam.
b2-17-01.english: Rumor has it that people in the city are laughing at me.
b2-17-01.canDo: I can report unverified information using úgy hírlik, hogy...

b2-17-02.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Signs Say
b2-17-02.scenario: Nero has read his informants' reports. He tells Seneca what he concludes from them.
b2-17-02.prompt: As Nero, tell Seneca what the signs show and who is most likely behind it.
cues: Say what you conclude from the signs
Say who is most likely behind it
b2-17-02.target: A jelek szerint valaki bajt akar okozni nekem, alighanem valaki a családomból.
b2-17-02.english: By all appearances someone wants to cause me trouble, most likely someone from my family.
b2-17-02.canDo: I can make reasoned inferences based on visible evidence using a jelek szerint

b2-17-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Who Says So
b2-17-03.scenario: Seneca asks Nero where he has his news from. Nero answers that he has it from the people who report to him.
b2-17-03.prompt: As Nero, tell Seneca whose account your news is based on.
b2-17-03.target: Az emberek elmondása alapján valaki bajt akar okozni nekem.
b2-17-03.english: Based on what people tell me, someone wants to cause me trouble.
b2-17-03.canDo: I can attribute statements to third parties using állításuk szerint and elmondása alapján

b2-17-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Check First
b2-17-04.scenario: Seneca advises Nero to be careful before he acts on the news.
b2-17-04.prompt: As Seneca, tell Nero that the news may not be true and that it must be checked.
cues: Say that it is possible that it is not true
b2-17-04.target: Nem kizárt, hogy a hír nem igaz, és még megerősítésre szorul.
b2-17-04.english: It is not ruled out that the news is not true, and it still needs confirmation.
b2-17-04.canDo: I can express epistemic doubt using kétséges, vajon...

b2-17-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Two Voices
b2-17-05.scenario: A friend at the palace asks you, one of Nero's advisers, what Nero and Seneca think of the news.
b2-17-05.prompt: Tell your friend how the two men see the news differently.
cues: Say what Seneca thinks, as a contrast
b2-17-05.target: Míg Nero szerint veszély van, addig Seneca szerint ez csak szóbeszéd.
b2-17-05.english: While according to Nero there is danger, according to Seneca this is only rumor.
b2-17-05.canDo: I can compare contradictory news reports using evidential distance markers

b2-17-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Rumor About the Poems
b2-17-consolidation.scenario: A friend in Rome asks you what is said about Nero's poems and whether it is true.
b2-17-consolidation.prompt: Tell your friend what is said and what is still unclear.
b2-17-consolidation.target: Úgy hírlik, hogy nevetnek Nero versén, de a hír még megerősítésre szorul.
b2-17-consolidation.english: Rumor has it that people are laughing at Nero's poem, but the news still needs confirmation.
b2-17-consolidation.canDo: I can distance claims using reportatives (úgy hírlik, állítólag) and deduce probability with inferentials (a jelek szerint, alighanem)
